newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close lower, seen hesitant.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close lower, seen hesitant.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed moderately lower Friday in a sluggish trading environment, following through on Thursday's reversal, dealers said.

"There's not much enthusiasm out there, even though the U.S. long bond yield continued to dip today and the Dow was very firm," one trader said. "Basically investors are skeptical about the trend abroad and are keeping a low profile, which made the bolsa lose the momentum that caused a rebound earlier this week."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 0.7 percent to 703.85, paring the week's gains to 2.6 percent.
Traders said Friday's options expirations also kept the market in check.

"The options deadline restricted price movements and pressured the market slightly downwards, although we can see that the 700 mark is still an important support level and the near-term outlook doesn't look too bad," said dealer Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro.
Floor volume remained weak at 19.5 million pesos against 19.2 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 77.6 million pesos from 102 million Thursday.
The broad market index closed off 0.5 percent, with losers overshooting winners 31 to 15 and 19 stocks closing flat.
The MerVal had dived 5.0 percent last week and stands 0.3 percent lower so far in April.
Friday's worst main-tier performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which reeled 10 percent, and carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, off 5.1 percent and 3.8 percent, respectively.
Strongest MerVal gainers were banks Banco de Galicia, Bansud and Banco Frances, which rose 1.8 percent, 1.5 percent and 1.1 percent, respectively, driven by bond sector gains.
